conventions.convention: Protocols use one fixed inertial frame, N ≥ 1 labels with fixed positive masses, an open configuration domain, and continuous force maps locally Lipschitz in the state locally uniformly in time. Every observation time must lie in every relevant unique maximal motion.

The readout may depend explicitly on both parameter and preparation labels. No readout regularity is assumed. The additive error takes values pointwise in an open domain containing zero; centering, moments, independence, and an error law are additional hypotheses.

Calibration settings select preparation slices through σ:C→Z. Nominal reference inputs, actual reference inputs, and reference-readout uncertainty are separate data. Mixed-unit deviations are compared using fixed positive coordinate scales.

Repeated observations use a fixed common prediction, n ≥ 1, and one error per repetition on a common probability space. IID means mutual independence and identical laws; finite second moment is separately adopted. Repetition indices run from 1 through n.

The pendulum is a separately adopted constrained model, not an instance of the open-domain force protocol. Its small-angle period relation is an idealization; finite-amplitude discrepancy is unbounded here. Covariance propagation is exact for the affine linearization, with nonlinear variance controlled separately using a fourth moment.

The frame-change sign is t′=t+b and x′=Rx+vt+a₀. The readout event moves to time t₁+b, and the additive position error transforms as Rε. A transformed force protocol requires an admissible fixed-domain presentation.
All example numbers and probability laws are declared hypothetical model data. No assigned item reports observations, measured uncertainties, or empirical confirmation.

load_bearing.statement: An operational observable model specifies parameter-indexed force maps, preparations assigning initial data, finite observation times lying in the unique maximal motions, a readout and its units, and observations Yθ,z=Φ(θ,z)+ε on a stated probability space with a declared open error domain.
Under the IID and second-moment hypotheses, E|Ȳ−μ|²=σ²/n and, for every a>0, P(|Ȳ−μ|≥a)≤σ²/(na²). These are adopted model hypotheses about repetitions, not consequences of the data.

Given the datum, the calibrated setting is c:=Γ(y,θref) and the calibrated prediction map is Φc. Reference-input and reference-readout uncertainty are specified separately and must both be carried into quantitative conclusions.

A test specifies a measurable rejection region, a probability family and a null set; size is the supremum of rejection probabilities over that null set. Rejection and retention concern the specified model, apparatus and sampling assumptions and do not prove a physical framework true or false.

A future reported experiment requires an actually retrieved primary report, setup, calibration, procedure, sampling, faithfully reported observations, uncertainty, and a specified comparison or inferential construction.

concerns.concern: The conventions say: “Independence of the errors fails when successive repetitions share a systematic effect ... or when the same recorded data are reused; identical distribution fails when the preparation or the conditions change between repetitions.” These are categorical implications not established by the definition and are false without further qualifications. For example, εk=b+Uk with a fixed common bias b and IID Bernoulli Uk remains IID despite the shared systematic effect. Reusing a deterministic reading also yields independent constant variables. Changed conditions need not change the observation law. The warning needs conditions under which dependence or differing laws actually follow.

“Changing the frame ... so the same physical protocol has a different prediction map in a different frame” overstates the conclusion for the arbitrary readout allowed by def-cm18-observable-model. A constant scalar readout, including the operational readout in the assigned finite-sample counterexample, can remain unchanged. Frame transformation must be specified, but it need not change every prediction map.

seams_checked.note: The mathematical supplier definitions and statements match the operational, calibration, finite-IID and inference uses. Centering and moments remain additional hypotheses; size, coverage and likelihood retain their specified-family meanings.

The finite-time bound retains tube, derivative, step and both-orbit retention assumptions. Numerical-map stability is distinguished from exact-field stability. Analytic energy bounds retain small-step, holomorphy and compact-retention hypotheses and make no exponential-time trajectory claim.

The electromagnetic bridge refers to mechanical quantities and conditional balances while retaining the declared interaction-structure and open-system qualifications; it imports no field momentum or combined conservation theorem.

Frame, worldline, unit, mass and Galilean sign conventions match the suppliers. The separate presentation concern concerns an assertion about arbitrary readouts, not a misquotation of the kinematic theorem.

Protocols preserve open-domain, positive-mass, continuity and state-local-Lipschitz hypotheses and explicitly require observation times inside the unique maximal motion. No global completeness is inferred.
The numerical remark uses the autonomous local flow as a partial map on its actual solution domain, without assuming completeness.

Pendulum sensitivity and covariance coefficients check algebraically. The Hessian bound controls the nonlinear remainder on the declared positive box; the variance correction uses its finite fourth moment. Uniform-motion sampling retains IID, finite second moment and zero-mean-error assumptions.
Position, velocity and units agree with the framework. Frame changes use t₁+b and RΦ+vt₁+a₀, rotate ε and its domain, and give covariance RΣRᵀ.

The zero-force examples satisfy the standing hypotheses and exhibit global motions directly. The pendulum is explicitly excluded from the open-domain force protocol. The frame example distinguishes general moving domains from admissible fixed-domain presentations.
